newsitem.title: UK: Social chapter a concern, but not yet - Nissan UK.
newsitem.headline: Social chapter a concern, but not yet - Nissan UK.

text.p: The European Union's social chapter on workplace standards is of potential future concern to Japanese car maker Nissan but has had no impact so far, a top manager of the firm's British operations said on Tuesday.

Ian Gibson, chief executive of Nissan Motor Manufacturing (UK) Ltd, told members of parliament that Nissan offered generous benefits at its Sunderland, northeast England, plant to attract and motivate a skilled workforce.
"The social chapter, insofar as it exists at present, ie legislation enacted, has zero effect on us," he told parliament's education and employment sub-committee.
"Our provisions in employment terms and conditions are ahead of those that have been legislated either in the UK or Europe," Gibson added.
But he said Nissan would have to examine any future social chapter regulations if and when they were introduced.

"I would not wish to suggest that the social chapter does not give rise to some concern... because, as I understand it, it is essentially enabling legislation and one thing any businessman likes to do is to understand the scale of the risk -- what the changes might be," Gibson said.
"So it does create a concern because it might lead to things that would reduce flexibility or impede flexibility," he added.

The social chapter is shaping up as an important issue in Britain's coming election because it is one of the few questions on which the ruling Conservative party and the main opposition Labour party are in fundamental disagreement.
Labour is committed to signing the chapter, saying good employers are in favour of high standards, but the Conservatives claim it would cost Britain half a million jobs.
